topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines its focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of innate immune sensing, including the characteristics of PAMPs and DAMPs alongside the genetic encoding and subcellular localization of pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail major classes of pattern recognition receptors and the inflammasome complex, explaining their ligand specificities and downstream inflammatory signaling pathways.

topics.label: Inflammatory response propagation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how sentinel cell activation drives leukocyte extravasation, lymphatic priming of adaptive immunity, and potentially fatal systemic inflammation such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammation, how tissues undergo healing and scarring, and the adaptations or pathologies resulting from chronic inflammatory persistence.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the complement system.
